questions.explain: Analytics on OLTP is a pricing mismatch: OLTP instances are priced for memory/IOPS (fast consistent transactions), while analytics needs CPU and sequential scan throughput — exactly what columnar MPP engines deliver far cheaper. Example: db.r5.4xlarge Multi-AZ ~$2,800/mo with 35% analytics time = ~$769/mo attributed to analytics; the same queries on Redshift Serverless = $90–$135/mo.

questions.explain: Classification from Query Store: mean execution >5 seconds AND average rows returned >10,000 → ANALYTICS_CANDIDATE; mean >1s and avg rows >1,000 → REVIEW_NEEDED. The dollar attribution: Performance Insights DB load by SQL digest × hourly instance cost gives analytics cost; when projected monthly analytics cost exceeds $500 consistently you have justification, at $2,000 the CTO conversation writes itself.

questions.explain: Three scenarios: (1) latency-tolerant batch on large volumes → Redshift Serverless / Synapse serverless / BigQuery (a 500GB Parquet scan in BigQuery = $2.50 flat; daily runs = $75/mo vs $840 RDS share); (2) near-real-time dashboards → readable Always On secondaries or Azure geo-replicas on a smaller instance; (3) ad-hoc analyst queries → Athena over daily S3 Parquet exports at $5/TB scanned (column pruning + Parquet means 90–95% less data scanned).

questions.explain: The three-layer savings stack: analytics offload + OLTP downsize + RI purchase — e.g., after removing analytics load, db.r6g.4xlarge → db.r6g.2xlarge ($2,196 → $1,098/mo, saving $1,098/mo), and a 1-year no-upfront RI on the 2xlarge is ~$686/mo (another 37% off). Combined with the analytics migration, total savings often land at $1,200–$1,800/mo per cluster.

Only the analytics migration saves money
